rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Referent resolution under a sequential deck read.

Chunk 5 line 42 "the second-pass read" is not named verbatim within this module file's own chunks 0-4, but this chunk sits `@after:extract-the-task-shaping-rule` per the transitions metadata, itself delivered after the inlined `exercises/push-back-on-the-plan.md`, which names "second-pass read"/"second-pass grilling" five times (grepped live: lines 5, 62, 68, 111, 235) — module + inlined exercise form one continuous deck by include-order, the same direction the compendium's own module-signposting carve-out already grants, so the term is established in the composed deck before the reader reaches it even though not literally in this .md source. rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Internal dialect never lands on a slide.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm rule prevents: repo/maintainer authoring jargon (surface-as-noun, firing, compendium, forcing function, beat, mood, Connections-as-proper-noun) reaching a slide the room can't parse. Mechanical: `grep -inE '\b(surface as noun|forcing function|firing|compendium|beat|mood|connections)\b'` over the whole body returns zero hits. Three judgment calls surfaced by the full-file read, none of them dialect: (1) chunk 7 line 73 "only the surface is new" — ordinary surface/depth metaphor (outward form vs. underlying skill), not our writing-surface content-type taxonomy term. (2) chunk 7 line 74 "where you put it decides when it fires" — describes real Claude Code CLAUDE.md loading mechanics using "fires" in its ordinary software sense (an event/trigger/hook fires), which the compendium's own §8 audience-register carve-out credits for AE101's engineer ICs; it teaches the student a real fact about rule-file activation, not maintainer meta-commentary about our compendium system. (3) chunk 10 line 101 "an external or user-facing surface" — standard security/engineering usage (attack surface / exposed surface), matching the security register of the M3 module it closes into, not our internal content-surface jargon. "Compound" (chunk 6 line 54) and "Boy Scout rule" (chunk 6 line 54) are both already covered by the file's own maintainer accept-notes as arc-earned spine vocabulary and a deliberately unattributed folk idiom respectively.

rules_evaluated.rule_lead: Emphasis budget — bold is for handles, and go very lightly.
rules_evaluated.evidence: Harm rule prevents: every bullet opening with a bolded full sentence, diluting bold's signal value. Full-body bold inventory (`grep -noE '\*\*[^*]+\*\*'` over body, 15 spans total): chunk 2 line 12 and chunk 10 line 103 are §34 mandated task-sizing anti-pattern callouts (maintainer-attested exemption, raw line 135) — the rule's own stated exception. Chunk 3 lines 18-22 are the five What-You'll-Learn LO verbs, the module-shape template's own bolded-verb shape — explicitly N/A per the rule's own text. Chunk 9 lines 89/91/93/97 ("Read:"/"Read:"/"Optional deeper scan:"/"Read:") are a reading-list/menu slide's mode-word labels — explicitly exempted by the rule's own carve-out ("bold the mode word alone... leave the title plain"), and each is 1-3 words. Chunk 4 line 26 "The question, to you:" is one 4-word kicker label, the chunk's only bolded element, within the ≤1-per-slide budget and the ≤5-word handle cap. Chunk 6 lines 56-58 ("Planning gaps."/"Conflicting information."/"Other context.") are three 2-word checklist-item-name handles — the rule's own handle definition explicitly credits "checklist item names" as valid bold content, same shape as the law/consolidation multi-handle carve-out. Every bolded span in the file resolves to an exempted category; none is a full-sentence lead. Open rule_question carried forward (not filed as REVISE, see rule_questions): should the stated carve-out say "law/consolidation OR checklist slide" explicitly, so a future judge doesn't have to re-derive it from the handle-definition sentence.

This target is a MODULE file; all 9 of its own `##` section headers (Big Idea, Prework, What You'll Learn, Start here, Save the rule if it earned itself, Leave the repo tidier than you found it, Key Concepts, Optional challenges, Pre-reads before Module N, Next) are module-level orientation/catalogue-style labels — the same family the rule explicitly carves out — not a governed exercise-imperative or lecture-claim slot. rule_questions: Rule 9's only stated multi-handle carve-out is "a law/consolidation slide may carry one handle per law," but the rule's own handle definition also lists "checklist item names" as valid bold content. `## Leave the repo tidier than you found it` bolds three 2-word checklist-item names (Planning gaps / Conflicting information / Other context) — same shape as the law carve-out (one short handle per named item), not the banned every-bullet-bold-sentence monoculture. Should the carve-out say "a law/consolidation OR checklist slide may carry one handle per item," so a future judge doesn't have to reason this from the handle-definition sentence each time?
